chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Cliff Jackson's band at the Nest and the long-haired professor pianist
summary: Personnel at the Nest and the pianist they called the Professor, who read everything and later went to Europe.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well now, wait a minute. Yeah, then you were with Cliff Jackson's band at the Nest, right?
At the Nest.
So who was in that band with you?
See, in that band we had Preacher Jones on trumpet. We had Bethel H. Burke and Manzie Johnson, when we broke in, Samson Edgar Simpson.
Oh. Well, they were just getting into things then.

They were all much younger, couple guys a little bit, but they were -- we had a nice experience because we all worked around together. Then Cliff got this group and this piano player went (unintelligible) to Europe, and -- oh, he came back -- very good piano player, read everything, all kind of Bach, Beethoven, play jazz too. And I was trying to call his name. He was Earl something, and we used to call him the professor because
he wore his hair long, a very light fellow, wore his hair long, we called him the professor. Said, Professor, what are you going to play? Cliff was concerned, very concerned because --
Oh, this piano player played with (unintelligible)?
Yeah. No, played with Cliff.
Well, Cliff was a piano player.
Yeah, but, see, Cliff didn't play with Snowden.
Oh, I see what you mean.

See, because he had Cliff (unintelligible) to get this other group. So Cliff said -- Cliff was very dry, you know -- Cliff said, let him play what he wants to play. He's a professor. We'd all sit there and laugh.
(Laughter)

I said, Cliff, why did you call him that? Isn't that what he is, Hap? I said, well if what did you say, the professor. Said, you could put up anything and read it. So he went to Europe, went to Paris. He stayed about two years and came back. I don't know what happened to that guy.
Now, I wonder who you were talking with there. See, that going -- there was a boy, Garnet Clark, went there, but he died, I think, in Europe, didn't he?
Yes, he did. I think he did.
Did you say his first name was Earl?

Think his first name was Earl. Cliff had all that stuff. We had -- I got to look that thing up in my book around at home, because he was a very good piano player, but we had those shows to play and entertainers, and you go in there and start to work at 11:00 o'clock, and you come out at 11:00 o'clock in the morning because it's, you know --
(Simultaneous remarks)
